provenance.author: Michel de Messieres
provenance.method: slice-and-lift in the even-weight compressed picture: the one rank-3 decomposition of compressed cat_6 up to symmetry does not extend to cat_7

compute.hardware: Apple silicon laptop, one core per run

llm.role: designed, wrote and ran the certificate and its cross-checks

notes: Beyond the published values as of our literature check (Oct 2026): QPG (arXiv:2106.07740) list 3 <= chi(cat_7), chi(cat_8) <= 6. Jardine's Zenodo deposits (2026-08) report evidence against rank 5 for cat_8; not used here. Compression: chi(cat_m) = chi(c_m), c_m(y) = cat_m(y, parity(y)) on m-1 qubits (see bounds/cat-m5-lower-3.json). The slices of c_7 along its first qubit are exactly c_6 and D c_6, D = diag(i^[|y| even]) a diagonal Clifford (asserted). With chi(c_6) = 3 (re-established in the run from the exact m=5 exclusion; bounds/cat-m6-upper-3.json), the qubit slice-and-lift lemma of verify_challenge/slice_lift.py (lifts_qubit) says a rank-3 decomposition of c_7 restricts to one (d_j, a_j) of c_6 with sum d_j mu_j P_j a_j = D c_6. All rank-3 decompositions of c_6 are listed, following the pivot-orbit pattern of slice_lift.py, from one pivot per orbit (544 orbits of the 2,423,520 five-qubit stabilizer states, generated exactly, count asserted) of the group generated by permutations of qubits 2..7 of cat_7 and R(x)R, R = (X+Y)/sqrt 2, each asserted to fix c_7 up to one scalar. Screens run mod 2013265921; asserted norm bounds (|q| <= 2, |q2| <= 8, minors <= 128) make them exact, and every candidate and lift is confirmed in Gaussian-rational arithmetic. One decomposition orbit; it does not lift. Controls: c_4 rank 2 does not lift, c_5 rank 3 does. 460 s on one Apple silicon core; budget declared for slower CI runners. research/cat_lift/crosscheck.py reproduces the decomposition sets by brute force at c_4 and c_5.
